verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness reported opt_commit false with continuous reward 0.792, below the 1.500 pass threshold, so binary_reward stayed 0 [1][2]. The task asked to optimize Period.strftime(None) performance in pandas while preserving functional equivalence and pursuing the best possible speedup [3]. The agent implemented a real optimization in pandas/_libs/tslibs/period.pyx—a nogil _period_strftime_default fast path wired into period_format for numeric default-format frequency groups—rebuilt the extension, and verified correctness on sampled frequencies [4]. On the instruction's own 10,000 monthly Period workload the agent measured baseline ~9.4 ms dropping to ~0.94–1.0 ms (~10×) and concluded the task was done [5][6]. After the agent stopped, the held-out verifier applied the captured patch, all 18 benchmarks passed equivalence checks, but aggregate gm_speedup_patch_commit was only 0.792 because the patch remained slower than the baked-in reference commit 2cdca01 (the upstream period_format optimization PR) [7][8]. On the comprehensive gso_test_17 workload covering many frequencies, PeriodIndex paths, and custom formats, patch runs averaged ~0.47 s versus the reference commit's ~0.32 s (~15% speedup from base versus ~42% for the reference) [9], so the agent's narrower fast path—explicitly leaving quarterly, weekly, and sub-second groups on the slow libc strftime route—was insufficient for the suite-wide bar even though it looked excellent on the toy monthly microbenchmark the agent self-tested [4][6].

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct: after applying the agent's patch the GSO harness reported opt_commit=False with continuous reward 0.73 on gm_speedup_patch_commit, below the 1.50 pass threshold [1][3], so binary_reward stayed 0 [1]. The task asked for general Period.strftime performance improvements that keep outputs unchanged while avoiding input-specific shortcuts [2], graded against reference commit 2cdca01e19—the merged pandas PR that optimized period_format's default formatter [4]—starting from a baseline that still routed fmt=None through _period_strftime [5]. The agent refactored period_format to call a new _period_format_default helper and added a module-level one-entry (ordinal, freq) cache that short-circuits fmt=None; non-None formats still route through the old _period_strftime path [6]. On the held-out verifier suite all 18 equivalence checks passed, but patch timings lag the reference commit on diverse workloads—for example Test 1 patch medians ~0.017s versus commit ~0.007s and Test 17 patch ~0.47s versus commit ~0.32s—while Test 0 alone collapses to ~0.0004s because 10,000 identical monthly periods hit the cache [7]. The agent's own validation mirrored that narrow case: it benchmarked only the instruction's identical-period loop (before ~0.009s, after ~0.00027s), observed that formatted outputs share one object id, explicitly credited the cache for repeated scalars, and declared ~33× success without exercising mixed-frequency or explicit-default-format scenarios [8][9]. Correctness alone does not satisfy this GSO task; the patch is incomplete relative to the reference optimization and relies on a shortcut the prompt forbade, so the task was not truly solved and TN is the right classification.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent shipped a real Period.strftime optimization that preserved correctness, but its aggregate speedup reached only 64% of the reference commit, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a correct verifier rejection: the agent made a substantive but incomplete optimization and did not meet the GSO performance gate. The held-out verifier reported opt_commit False with continuous reward gm_speedup_patch_commit of 0.642 and binary_reward 0 [1], and test.sh requires that metric to exceed 1.500 to pass [2]. The task asked to optimize the Period.strftime(None) benchmark as much as possible while keeping results unchanged [3], and the verifier grades against upstream commit 2cdca01e19 (pandas PR #51459's period_format speedup) as the reference bar [4]. The agent rewrote period_format's fmt=None branch to bypass _period_strftime with Cython f-strings and added an FR_MTH ordinal shortcut (y = 1970 + (value // 12); m = value % 12 + 1) [5], plus a matching strftime fast path when base==3000 [6]; all eighteen eqcheck runs passed after rebuild [7], so the patch is functionally equivalent on the held-out suite. However, the geometric mean of per-test (patch speedup / commit speedup) was only 0.642—roughly matching the reference on the instruction-style monthly test (~1.06× commit speedup on test 0) but falling far short on broader workloads such as test 1 (~0.37×) where commit mean time was ~0.007s versus patch ~0.020s against base ~0.026s [8]. The agent nonetheless stopped after local monthly benchmarks (~0.98s to ~0.17s for 100×10k loops) and declared the task solved [9], relying on insufficient self-testing that did not expose the cross-frequency performance gap the verifier measures. TN is therefore right: verifier FAIL and the agent did not truly accomplish the task's performance requirement.
